newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kuehbacher - Germany, France will not meet EMU goals.
newsitem.headline: Kuehbacher - Germany, France will not meet EMU goals.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher said on Monday that neither Germany or France would meet the government debt and deficit criteria in 1997 for membership of European currency union.
Kuehbacher, also head of the state central bank in Berlin and Brandenburg, said in Potsdam that tax revenues, figures for which are expected this month, would undershoot estimates in Germany.
He also said France was unlikely to meet the two key criteria.

He was referring to Maastricht treaty criteria which require that European Union member nations aim for budget deficits of no more than three percent of gross domestic product and a government debt of no more than 60 percent of GDP in 1997 to join EMU at its launch.
Kuehbacher said he did not rule out tax increases in Germany in this context.
Earlier Kuehbacher called for close adherence to the entry criteria for European currency union.
